claims.text: Increasing Cr content in CoCrFeMnNi from about 15 at.% to about 25 at.% enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The improved oxidation resistance is caused by formation and retention of a uniform Cr-rich oxide, such as Cr2O3.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is equiatomic.
The baseline alloy contains approximately 15 at.% Cr.
Cr concentration will be varied from 15 at.% to 25 at.% while the other elemental concentrations remain constant.
Oxidation will be tested in dry air at 900–1100 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressure.
The relevant structural mediator is a continuous and adherent Cr-rich surface layer composed primarily of Cr2O3.
A Cr-rich Cr2O3 layer acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
Chromium has a higher redox potential and favorable oxidation kinetics that drive preferential oxidation at the alloy surface.
Increasing bulk Cr increases the driving force for selective Cr oxidation.
A dense protective Cr2O3 scale minimizes oxygen diffusion into the substrate.
The approximately 25 at.% Cr alloy will form a more uniform, adherent, and slower-growing Cr-rich oxide than the approximately 15 at.% Cr alloy.
The higher-Cr alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain and less oxide spallation than the baseline.
The approximately 15 at.% Cr baseline will form less continuous or non-protective oxides and consequently show higher oxidation rates and weight gains.
The proposed mechanism applies over 900–1100 °C in dry air with controlled oxygen partial pressure.
Humidity or competing alloying effects may alter the oxidation mechanism or kinetics.
The mechanism is falsified if increased Cr produces neither a significantly improved Cr-rich oxide layer nor improved weight-gain and spallation behavior relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: A five-component equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy would contain approximately 20 at.% of each element, which conflicts with describing the same baseline as containing approximately 15 at.% Cr.

Increasing Cr from 15 to 25 at.% while keeping all other elemental atomic percentages constant is compositionally impossible because the atomic percentages would no longer sum to 100; the balancing changes are not specified.
